Shit, there's probably more than a few. Always has been. Snowden just decided to (and successfully did) take credit for what dozens of people have been doing in secret for years, and he's paying the price for being so public with his actions. But so are we, if you give it more than a few seconds of critical thought.

I worked for one of those agencies when the whole Snowden thing went down -- not the NSA, but one of its cousins -- and I watched the 15s lose their shit over activities everyone else knew were going on day-in and day-out. Prior to Snowden, camera-equipped smartphones with USB ports were allowed in my building; not the scif, mind you, but you can imagine that having something so useful so ubiquitous was helpful to anyone who wanted to point out problems with the system. After Snowden... anyone caught with so much as a USB cable in their lunchbox was put on leave for the first offense, and banned from all US government installations for life on the second offense -- I watched it happen.

Snowden may have confirmed a lot of what everyone already knew to be true, and maybe he should be commended for giving a few Senators the paperwork they needed to actually level charges, as impotent as they are, against the people involved, but in the long run, he made the act of uncovering the truth of these matters way, way harder... or at least proving it.

How often has a leaker made his activities as public as Snowden has? Almost all of them try to hide their identities, either to protect themselves or enable further leaks. Snowden, on the other hand, announced his identity almost as quickly as possible - and made himself famous in the process. He claimed he it did to protect his teammates and encourage further leakers, but he had to have known the resulting crackdown would only make things harder.

I've said before that making himself a hero would be the best protection for any malicious espionage, but it could also be the other way: securing vital defense documents would make countries like Russia more open to protecting him while he stroked his ego.
